title: Frobenius acts on roots of unity by the q-th power
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, and $k$ an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; let $\varphi_q\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, $z\mapsto z^q$, be the arithmetic Frobenius and $\gamma=\varphi_q^{-1}$ the geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Let $N\geq1$ be an integer prime to $p$ and $\mu_N(k)=\{\zeta\in k^\times:\zeta^N=1\}$. Then:

1. $\mu_N(k)$ is a cyclic group of order $N$, and every automorphism $\sigma$ of the field $k$ maps $\mu_N(k)$ to itself.
2. $\varphi_q(\zeta)=\zeta^q$ and $\gamma(\zeta)=\zeta^{q'}$ for every $\zeta\in\mu_N(k)$, where $q'\in\mathbf Z$ is any integer with $qq'\equiv1\pmod N$ (it exists since $\gcd(q,N)=1$).
3. Let $\ell\neq p$ be a prime and $T_\ell\mu(k)=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r}(k)$, the limit along the maps $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^\ell$. It is a free $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module of rank one [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] (written additively), $\varphi_q$ and $\gamma$ act on it componentwise, and $\varphi_q$ acts as multiplication by $q\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$ and $\gamma$ as multiplication by $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z_\ell^\times$.

source.place: (2.2), p. 281: 'si k = F_q, la substitution de Frobenius phi : x -> x^q agit [sur Q_l(1)] par multiplication par q'; the geometric Frobenius F = phi^{-1}: literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf, (1.1.7), pp. 150-151

proof.text: Recover CharP k₀ p from the cardinality q=p^a and transfer it to k along the injective algebra map. Coprimality gives NeZero (N : k). Apply [lem-sc-primitive-root] to obtain a primitive N-th root, hence the cardinality N; rootsOfUnity.isCyclic gives cyclicity. A field automorphism preserves the equation ζ^N=1 by map_pow and map_one. Its inverse supplies a preimage, and injectivity on units follows from injectivity on the field.

source.place: first paragraph: arithmetic Frobenius sends each root of unity to its q-th power

proof.text: By [def-weil-frobenius-substitution] and the equality card(k₀)=q, arithmetic Frobenius F satisfies F(x)=x^q. Coprimality of q=p^a with N and the integer Bezout identity give q′=Nat.gcdA q N with qq′ congruent to 1 modulo N. For any such q′ and ζ in μ_N, orderOf ζ divides N, so zpow_eq_zpow_iff_modEq gives ζ^(qq′)=ζ. Applying the injective unit map induced by F identifies F⁻¹(ζ) with ζ^q′.

source.place: second paragraph: inverse of q modulo each ℓ^n and the inverse automorphism

proof.text: Put M=Additive(kˣ). For each x in kˣ, [def-weil-algebraic-closure] supplies y with y^ℓ=x; y is nonzero, so it defines a unit and proves surjectivity of multiplication by ℓ on M. Explicitly identify the subtype M[ℓ] with rootsOfUnity ℓ k by the ofMul/toMul equivalence. The primitive-root count from [lem-sc-primitive-root] gives cardinality ℓ. Apply [lem-av-tate-module-group-rank] with r=1 and then evaluate Fin 1 → ℤ_[ℓ] at its unique index. This gives the required linear equivalence for the Tate module of [def-tate-module-abelian-group].

source.place: slopmaster2 read-only source, theorem AddCommGroup.tateModule.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_natCard_eq, lines 228–230: specialize to M=Additive(k^×) and r=1; divisibility and torsion-cardinality hypotheses verified explicitly in this step

proof.text: For ℓ≠p, q=p^a is coprime to ℓ. PadicInt.norm_natCast_eq_one_iff and PadicInt.isUnit_iff make the scalar q a unit u. On each coordinate of the Tate module [def-tate-module-abelian-group], coe_map_apply and F(x)=x^q identify the arithmetic action with q-fold addition. The coordinate scalar formula coe_smul_apply and appr_zsmul_coe_eq identify this with the canonical ℤ_[ℓ]-action of q. The composition of the coordinatewise maps induced by F and F⁻¹ is the identity. Replace the arithmetic action in this identity by u and multiply by u⁻¹; the scalar associativity and unit cancellation give the required inverse action.

source.place: second paragraph: compatible inverses define q^{-1} in ℤ_ℓ and the inverse automorphism acts by q^{-1}

proof_origin.place: Complete proof, paragraphs 1–2; formalized by R2 using the existing primitive-root and Tate-module rank declarations. The inverse scalar action follows directly from composition with arithmetic Frobenius rather than constructing inverse residues.

lean.statement: theorem frobenius_rootsOfUnity_power (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hNp : N.Coprime D.p) : (IsCyclic (rootsOfUnity N D.k) ∧ Nat.card (rootsOfUnity N D.k) = N ∧ ∀ σ : D.k ≃+* D.k, Set.BijOn (Units.map σ.toRingHom.toMonoidHom) (rootsOfUnity N D.k) (rootsOfUnity N D.k)) ∧ ((∀ ζ : rootsOfUnity N D.k, (@FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic D.k₀ _ (Fintype.ofFinite D.k₀) D.k _ _ _) ((ζ : D.kˣ) : D.k) = ((ζ : D.kˣ) : D.k) ^ D.q) ∧ (∃ q' : ℤ, Int.ModEq (N : ℤ) ((D.q : ℤ) * q') 1) ∧ ∀ q' : ℤ, Int.ModEq (N : ℤ) ((D.q : ℤ) * q') 1 → ∀ ζ : rootsOfUnity N D.k, Units.map (@FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic D.k₀ _ (Fintype.ofFinite D.k₀) D.k _ _ _).symm.toRingHom.toMonoidHom (ζ : D.kˣ) = (ζ : D.kˣ) ^ q') ∧ (∀ (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime], ℓ ≠ D.p → Nonempty (AddCommGroup.tateModule ℓ (Additive D.kˣ) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[ℓ]] ℤ_[ℓ]) ∧ ∃ u : ℤ_[ℓ]ˣ, (u : ℤ_[ℓ]) = (D.q : ℤ_[ℓ]) ∧ ∀ t : AddCommGroup.tateModule ℓ (Additive D.kˣ), AddCommGroup.tateModule.map (Units.map (@FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic D.k₀ _ (Fintype.ofFinite D.k₀) D.k _ _ _).toRingHom.toMonoidHom).toAdditive t = (u : ℤ_[ℓ]) • t ∧ AddCommGroup.tateModule.map (Units.map (@FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic D.k₀ _ (Fintype.ofFinite D.k₀) D.k _ _ _).symm.toRingHom.toMonoidHom).toAdditive t = (↑(u⁻¹) : ℤ_[ℓ]) • t)
